hero.title: Anda Foundation
hero.subtitle: The Philosophy of the Eternal Sky
hero.description: A path guided by oaths, honor, determination, and the courage to begin again.

about.title: What is Anda?
about.paragraph1: Anda is a life philosophy that finds its origins in the ancient traditions of the steppe. The word "anda" means "oath" or "covenant" and symbolized deep loyalty, often stronger than blood ties. In modern times, Anda offers a new perspective: a covenant with yourself, an inner promise to live with courage, uncertainty, compassion, and reverence for nature.
about.paragraph2: The Anda Foundation aims to spread and materialize this philosophy. Not as dogma, but as an invitation to dialogue, reflection, and community building. We build bridges between tradition and modernity, between spirituality and science, between nature and humanity.

pillars.title: The Six Pillars of Anda
pillars.intro: The core of the Anda philosophy rests on six pillars. Together they form a compass for an honest, courageous, and connected life.

pillar1.title: Nomadism
pillar1.description: Always in motion, physically and mentally. A nomad continues to learn, discover, and renew.

pillar2.title: A Straight Back
pillar2.description: Honesty, courage, and sportsmanship as guidance, inspired by the discipline of the samurai.

pillar3.title: Infinity
pillar3.description: The Eternal Sky as a symbol of connection and spirituality.

pillar4.title: Uncertainty
pillar4.description: Recognition that there are no absolute truths. Learning to live with our own uncertainties and broader uncertainty.

pillar5.title: Reverence for Nature
pillar5.description: Nature as a sanctuary and mirror of our inner life. Reverence brings connection.

pillar6.title: Intention
pillar6.description: Imperfections make us unique. Like cracks in a vase repaired with gold, scars are part of beauty. No one can be the ideal human being, it's about the intention.

sky.title: Under the Eternal Sky
sky.quote: We are not superior, not inferior. We are who we are. One with the Eternal Sky.
sky.description: Anda invites you to acknowledge uncertainty, honor nature, and embrace imperfections as part of who you are. The Eternal Sky is a metaphor for infinity, for diversity and connection.

skyyurt.title: Skyyurts & Skystones
skyyurt.paragraph1: The Skyyurt is a space of silence and connection, inspired by the simplistic lifestyle of the steppe peoples. Here people come together for meditation, dialogue, and drinking a cup of warm tea. Among countless warm carpets.
skyyurt.paragraph2: Skystones are stone pillars with inscriptions that remind us of universal values such as courage, compassion, honesty, and reverence for nature. Together they form physical symbols of the Anda philosophy.

mission.title: Mission & Vision
mission.paragraph1: The Anda Foundation aims to build communities grounded in honor, honesty, compassion, and mutual support. Through Ands, we encourage people to live with purpose, take responsibility, and remain true to their oaths, even after failure.
mission.paragraph2: Our vision is a more equal world where people live with honor, embrace uncertainty, respect nature, and stand by their oaths. A world where we support one another, learn from our failures, and continue moving forward.

boodschap.metaDescription: The message of Anda: a covenant not with another, but with yourself. Anda Foundation explains the steppe tradition behind the oath.
boodschap.title: The Message of Anda
boodschap.paragraph1: On the ancient steppe, there exists a tradition. This tradition is called "anda".
boodschap.paragraph2: The word "and" means oath or vow in the languages of the steppe peoples. From this word, "anda" is derived: a covenant between two people who trusted each other so deeply that they swore to consider each other as brother or sister. Such bonds were forged only once in a lifetime and remained valid forever. They were often sealed with blood. Both persons cut into their palms with the blade of their sword and swore loyalty to each other.
boodschap.paragraph3: This philosophy, the Anda, is also a covenant.
boodschap.paragraph4: But not a covenant with another.
boodschap.paragraph6: A set of principles that are not necessarily the absolute truth – because part of this philosophy is precisely the recognition of uncertainty – but a collection of beliefs that you, somewhere deep in your heart, feel are right and for which you want to live.
boodschap.paragraph7: And perhaps, someday, will want to swear by.

eed.metaDescription: The And is the oath of Anda Foundation: vows to live as a nomad, with a straight back, at one with infinity and with reverence for nature.
eed.title: The And – The Oath
eed.oath1: I swear that I will be a nomad, my heart open to everyone.
eed.oath2: I swear that I will live with my eyes fixed on the Eternal Sky, shoulders straight, honorably, with a healthy body and a clear mind.
eed.oath3: I swear that I will become one with Infinity.
eed.oath4: I swear that I will learn to live with uncertainty.
eed.oath5: I swear that I will have reverence for nature and that I will leave the world greener.
eed.oath6: I swear that I will not hide my wrinkles and cracks, because this does not make me less, but only more.
eed.oathFinal: I swear it, I swear, I swear it.

pilaren.metaDescription: Nomadism, a straight back, infinity, uncertainty, reverence for nature and intention: the six pillars of Anda Foundation, each explained in full.

pillar1.title: Pillar 1: Nomadism
pillar1.short: Not all who wander are lost. Not all who walk multiple paths have lost their way.
pillar1.full:
Not all who wander are lost.
Not all who walk multiple paths have lost their way.
Not everyone who moves into another is losing themselves.
A leader of Anda is a nomad, both in lifestyle and in ideology.
A nomad is someone who opens their heart to different cultures, customs, countries, and people.
A nomad is someone who does not stand still but continues to innovate and challenge themselves.
A nomad is someone who can live on a piece of bread but can also enjoy a plate of delicious dishes.
A nomad is someone whose heart beats faster when exploring new places.
A nomad is someone who can be fully present in the now, even though they know this is very difficult.
We, as leaders of Anda, are nomads.
When we stay in one place too long, our feet start to itch.
Then we are asked to carve a new path for ourselves.
We are one with the Eternal Sky. And wherever the Eternal Sky is, there we are.

pillar2.title: Pillar 2: A Straight Back
pillar2.short: Honesty. Your shoulders straight and your chest forward. Eyes on the Eternal Sky.
pillar2.full:
Honesty.
Your shoulders straight and your chest forward.
Eyes on the Eternal Sky.
That is the mantra of a leader of Anda.
Someone who acknowledges their insecurities and shortcomings.
Someone who tries to find peace with themselves.
Someone who does not help others to feel good about themselves, but to be stronger together.
Someone who dares to extend a helping hand to their family, neighbors, even people they dislike.
Someone who tries to be a good person, no matter what, despite their past and their sins.
This pillar is inspired by the philosophy of the samurai. They held their honor as their highest banner, their pride, and were even willing to commit harakiri (suicide) for this philosophy.
Let this be completely clear: Anda absolutely and resolutely rejects the harakiri of Bushido. However, we take the other positive aspects of Bushido as inspiration. Hence this pillar bears the name "Positive Bushido".
These are the following values:

1. Courage
2. Honor
3. Sportsmanship
4. Honesty
5. A healthy body and a strong mind

pillar3.title: Pillar 3: Infinity
pillar3.short: Earth is not the only planet. There are billions.
pillar3.full:
Earth is not the only planet.
There are billions.
The Eternal Sky is not seen by leaders of Anda as a God or person, but as an energy: an infinity of thoughts, planets, ideas, people, and nature.
In moments of stress and negativity, we do not try to keep these thoughts at a distance, but to acknowledge, illuminate, understand them – to become one.
When we make music, sing, we become one with the people you hate, despise – we become one with love, peace, and infinity.
Just as a hand has multiple fingers, a leader of Anda believes that people can reach this Infinity, this Eternal Sky, in multiple ways.
This can be by believing in a God or Gods, with different religions, ideas, philosophies, or not believing in a God at all.
We, as leaders of Anda, are not superior, but we are also not inferior.
We are who we are,
One with the Eternal Sky.
One with people of different origins, blood, color, or descent.
Our heart is open to everyone who also opens their own heart.

pillar4.title: Pillar 4: Uncertainty
pillar4.short: This world, our lives, could be a simulation in the game of a God.
pillar4.full:
Our thoughts could be part of a dream. The planets, stars, and universe could be an illusion. Everything we understand about existence may be incomplete, mistaken, or entirely different from what we imagine. Even the origins of existence may lie beyond anything the human mind can comprehend.

Mengü, the Eternal Sky, represents the infinity beyond our understanding. Yet Andaism acknowledges that even Mengü may not exist as we imagine it. The Eternal Sky could be an illusion, a human invention, a shared fantasy, or something entirely different from what we believe. Even the sacred center of Andaism is not exempt from uncertainty.

An Anda may choose to believe in Mengü, but must never confuse that belief with absolute knowledge. No religion, philosophy, or ideology can conclusively eliminate every possibility of uncertainty about the ultimate nature of existence.

This is one of the central teachings of Andaism: we do not follow Mengü because we know with certainty that Mengü is real. We follow Mengü because the Eternal Sky gives us a way to approach the unknown, find meaning in existence, and live more peacefully within it.

Ands is our chosen path beneath that uncertainty. Through our oaths, we strive to grow closer to Mengü and to become endless, not by discovering every answer, but by learning to live without needing them all.

Acknowledging uncertainty does not make us weaker. Nor does it necessarily make us stronger. We simply recognize it for what it is, without shame, fear, or the need to disguise belief as knowledge.

Even if Mengü were nothing more than a human dream, the life we live beneath that dream would remain real to us. And that life is worth living fully.

pillar5.title: Pillar 5: Reverence for Nature
pillar5.short: Touching a tree and closing your eyes, isn't that weird? Not for a leader of Anda.
pillar5.full:
We are part of nature, and nature is part of us.
Walking in nature is preferably done alone.
Little sound, little distraction.
Just you, nature, and the Eternal Sky.
Nature will not be a healer of all your problems and rampant thoughts.
That is also something a person of Anda learns to acknowledge.
Nature is like a sanctuary. Sometimes you do not find the comfort you came searching for, and it will sometimes confront you with the very thoughts you wished to escape, but that too is part of its sacred wisdom, and it always remains a place to return to. There you can let your thoughts and your soul run free and you learn to know yourself better.
A leader of Anda likes to plant trees, maintain their garden, constantly spread seeds of plants and trees, learn about nature, and explore ways to survive in the wild.
Because we are one.

pillar6.title: Pillar 6: Intention
pillar6.short: Imperfections make us unique. Like cracks in a vase repaired with gold, scars are part of beauty. No one can be the ideal human being, it's about the intention.
pillar6.full:
This last pillar is based on the principles of Kintsugi. The leaders of Anda understand that imperfection is part of life.
A leader of Anda does not strive for perfection but understands that perfection only exists in utopias and stories. A leader of Anda will never reach nirvana by following these pillars. On the contrary, they will often have difficulty executing certain pillars or may forget certain principles.
Sometimes they get distracted by other matters – temptations or desires – things they don't actually stand for.
However, we understand as leaders of Anda that this is part of imperfection.
Just as a pimple or disability does not make someone ugly – we learn to look beneath the layers, to smile – deeper into the soul.
We extend a hand to people, regardless of what profession they practice, to better understand them and follow a path together.
Similar principles are taught by Kintsugi. It is an ancient art form in which imperfections are celebrated: the cracks in a vase are seen as part of the object's history, rather than something that must be hidden.

statuten.metaDescription: The statutes of Anda Foundation: its name and seat, purpose, means, assets, board, annual accounts, policy plan and dissolution.
statuten.subtitle: The Philosophy of the Eternal Sky

transparency.title: Transparency & Annual Reports
transparency.paragraph1: Anda Foundation stands for honesty, clarity, and trust. Like the Bushido warrior who guards his honor, we publish our annual accounts, policy plan, statements, and bank transactions every year.
transparency.paragraph2: We believe that only complete openness enables a sustainable and spiritual community. This way, everyone always knows how our resources are spent, in service of our mission and the Eternal Sky.

article1.title: Article 1 – Name and Seat
article1.content: The foundation bears the name: Anda Foundation – The Philosophy of the Eternal Sky. It may also present itself under the shortened name Anda Foundation. The foundation has its seat in the municipality of Delft, Netherlands.

article2.title: Article 2 – Purpose
goals: Promote philosophical, spiritual, cultural, and social research and dialogue, inspired by Anda.
Stimulate reflection on the relationship between humans, nature, and cosmos.
Contribute to communities where honesty, compassion, and connection are central.
Promote understanding of spiritual and philosophical diversity.
article2.conclusion: The foundation operates without profit motive and meets the requirements for ANBI status.

article3.title: Article 3 – Means
article3.intro: The foundation seeks to achieve its goal through:
means: Organizing lectures, conferences, retreats, and dialogues.
Publishing books, essays, podcasts, and artistic expressions.
Realizing and managing Skyyurts and Skystones.
Entering into collaborations with educational institutions and social organizations.
Raising funds, donations, legacies, and subsidies.

article4.title: Article 4 – Assets
article4.content: The foundation's assets are formed by subsidies, donations, gifts, inheritances, legacies, and proceeds from activities. All resources are used exclusively for the objectives. Board members receive no remuneration, only attendance fees and expense reimbursement.

article5.title: Article 5 – Board
article5.content: The board consists of at least one person. Functions can be divided (chairman, secretary, treasurer). Appointments are for four years and renewable. The board guards the foundation's objectives and inspiration.

article6.title: Article 6 – Representation
article6.content: The foundation is represented by the board collectively. For legal acts exceeding €25,000, approval from the entire board is required.

article7.title: Article 7 – Meetings and Decision-making
article7.content: The board meets at least twice a year. Minutes are taken of each meeting. Decisions are made by majority vote.

article8.title: Article 8 – Annual Accounts and Transparency
article8.paragraph1: The financial year coincides with the calendar year. Within six months, the board approves and signs the annual accounts. The foundation publicly publishes its annual accounts, policy plan, and statements.
article8.paragraph2: In addition, we also annually publish our bank transactions. We do this out of conviction that a foundation can only exist through honesty, clarity, and complete transparency – like a Bushido warrior guards his honor.

article9.title: Article 9 – Policy Plan and Accountability
article9.content: Annually, the board establishes a policy plan with goals, activities, and budget. The foundation publicly accounts for activities and expenditure of resources.

article10.title: Article 10 – Dissolution
article10.content: Dissolution can be decided by the board with a two-thirds majority. Any positive balance goes to an ANBI institution with similar objectives.

article11.title: Article 11 – Final Provisions
article11.content: In cases not provided for in these statutes, the board decides. Changes are possible with a two-thirds majority.

skyyurt.metaDescription: Skyhaven, the planned project of Anda Foundation: a Skyyurt for silence, a Skystone bearing the oath and the Nomad's Heart café, open to all by 2030.
skyyurt.heroDescription: A future project of Anda Foundation. Planned for 2030 and made possible through support and donations.
skyyurt.introParagraph1: The Skyyurt, the Skystone, and the Nomad’s Heart café together form the Skyhaven project of Anda Foundation. This project does not yet exist, but it is our heartfelt intention and commitment to bring it to life in 2030 at a special place in the Netherlands.
skyyurt.introParagraph2: With this initiative we want to create a free and welcoming space in nature: a meditation place where everyone is welcome — regardless of religion, worldview, or background — and where silence is not something you have to buy, but something you are invited to remember.
skyyurt.introParagraph3: It will be a place to be with yourself for a while. To meet your thoughts and feelings gently, without judgment. A space to breathe, slow down, and reconnect with yourself and with nature.
skyyurt.skyyurtTitle: The Skyyurt – Silence under the Eternal Sky
skyyurt.skyyurtParagraph: The Skyyurt is inspired by the traditional round tents of steppe peoples. Its interior is fully covered with nomadic carpets and cushions. The space is open to all religions and worldviews, and is meant to be a public place of stillness in Dutch nature.
skyyurt.skyyurtFeature1: No chairs — everyone sits equally in the circle.
skyyurt.skyyurtFeature3: Maximum stay of 60 minutes per person.
skyyurt.skystoneTitle: The Skystone – The And in Stone
skyyurt.skystoneParagraph: Beside the Skyyurt rises the Skystone: a natural stone pillar about 2.5 meters high. The And — the Oath — will be engraved into it as a lasting symbol of loyalty, connection, and inner strength.
skyyurt.skystoneQuote: I swear that I will be a nomad, my heart open to everyone…
skyyurt.nomadsHeartParagraph: Where the Skyyurt brings silence and the Skystone anchors devotion, Nomad’s Heart offers warmth and encounter: a café for dialogue, philosophy, faith, and conversations about mental well-being.
skyyurt.nomadsHeartFeature1: A safe space for mental and emotional challenges.
skyyurt.nomadsHeartFeature2: Furnished like a living room with rugs, tea, and books.
skyyurt.nomadsHeartFeature3: A bridge between inwardness and dialogue.
skyyurt.purposeIntro: Anda Foundation is building something the Netherlands still largely lacks: a spiritual and meditative home in nature, open to everyone — without religious barriers, membership, or a price tag on silence.
skyyurt.purposePoint1Title: Open spirituality, without a religious gate
skyyurt.purposePoint1Text: A place for people of any belief — or none. No sacred language, no compulsory teaching, no single “right way.” Only room to be.
skyyurt.purposePoint2Text: Designed as a respectful, calm environment for women and men alike, where safety and dignity come first.
skyyurt.purposePoint3Text: Alongside stillness, there is warmth. We host evenings by the fire with music, stories, and singing — even if you’ve never sung before.
skyyurt.purposePoint4Text: A space where cultures and philosophies meet without one tradition dominating. Not a closed community; everyone is welcome with openness and respect.
skyyurt.purposePoint5Title: Refuge from work and digital noise
skyyurt.purposePoint5Text: In Nomad’s Heart you can read, sit quietly, or work on your laptop. There will be plugs and laptop-friendly spots where time is never a debt.
skyyurt.purposePoint6Text: A place to write and share in the footsteps of Rumi, Yunus Emre, Hadewijch, Thomas à Kempis, and other spiritual poets.
skyyurt.purposePoint7Text: Outdoor space for tai chi, yoga, breathwork, and a simple calisthenics gym — where inner peace and physical strength support each other.
skyyurt.purposePoint8Text: The Skyyurt is meant as a gift to society: low-threshold, donation-supported, and especially welcoming to those who often feel excluded from spiritual spaces.
skyyurt.purposeConclusion: Ultimately, the Skyyurt is an invitation to slow down — to breathe again, listen inwardly, and reconnect with nature and community.
skyyurt.donationParagraph: The Skyyurt, Skystone, and Nomad’s Heart do not yet exist. These plans become reality thanks to donations and support. Every contribution brings us closer to the first realization in 2030.
skyyurt.donationComingSoon: Donation functionality will be available soon!

bankafschriften.conclusion: This choice is unusual, but fits our philosophy: honest and transparent, like a Bushido warrior guards his honor.

openheid.metaDescription: Why Anda Foundation publishes everything: statutes, annual reports, bank statements and plans, as an example of radical transparency.
openheid.subtitle: Why the Anda Foundation publishes everything
openheid.paragraph1: In a world where foundations and organizations are often distrusted, Anda chooses radical transparency. We want to be an example: a foundation that has nothing to hide, but shows how it acts, in accordance with its values.
openheid.paragraph2: Every euro you donate to us is visible in our bank statements. Every plan we make is described in our policy documents. Every idea we share is recorded in books and essays. This is our way of being faithful to our oath: honesty, courage, and compassion.
openheid.paragraph3: Anda Foundation believes in openness, simplicity, and honesty. On the pages below you will find all documents that our foundation consciously and voluntarily makes public. We believe that true spirituality goes hand in hand with transparency: nothing behind closed doors, but visible and verifiable for everyone. This way, everyone can see with their own eyes how we work, where the money comes from, and how we spend it on our mission.

contact.heroDescription: A bridge between philosophy, community, and innovation. Reach us and become part of the dialogue under the Eternal Sky.
contact.aboutFoundationParagraph1: Anda Foundation is committed to translating the ancient Anda philosophy to modern society. From our home base in Delft, we build bridges between spirituality, science, art, and community.
contact.aboutFoundationParagraph2: We organize lectures, dialogues, cultural projects, and workshops that invite reflection and connection. Our mission is to create places of silence and encounter, where people come together to embrace uncertainty and cultivate reverence for nature.
contact.approachParagraph1: Our projects always grow from dialogue and collaboration. We believe that real change does not arise from theory alone, but from encounter and practice in daily life.
contact.approachParagraph2: From Delft, we work on initiatives that connect art, culture, and community. This ranges from intimate workshops to large-scale cultural projects, always with room for reflection and imagination.
contact.approachParagraph3: Our goal is to create places of inspiration and connection, where people learn together, discover new perspectives, and care for each other and nature.
contact.partnershipsIntro: We are always looking for partners who share our vision: universities, cultural institutions, spiritual centers, governments, and companies with a heart for sustainability, art, and humanity.

contact.partnershipsArea2: Community: collaborations with local and international networks.
contact.partnershipsArea3: Art & Culture: exhibitions, performances, and creative projects.
